name: Ge
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Sun, Jin 2020. Qian dongnan feng xiang (ren ge) yu ge'an yanjiu (117pp phonology/text study of Ge); Hutton 1937 — neither reachable online

sources.citation: Chen Qiguang 陈其光 2013 苗瑶语文 — data-point list checked via lexibank/chenhmongmien CLDF.
sources.note: No 重安江/枫香/亻革 data point in Chen 2013, so it is not a Ge source.

sources.citation: en.wikipedia 'Gejia language'; zh.wikipedia '𱎼家话' (wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Classification/distribution only; nothing on stress. Cite Chen Xueyu 2011 MA and HZYYC 2017 p.40.

sources.citation: Sun Hongkai 孙宏开, Ding Bangxin 丁邦新, Jiang Di 江荻 & Yan Haixiong 燕海雄 (eds.). 2017. 汉藏语语音和词汇 Hanzangyu yuyin he cihui. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. p.40 and pp.152-153 '苗语枫香话音位系统简介'.
sources.note: Silent. Fengxiang 枫香寨 (Chong'an township, Huangping) = representative point of 重安江次方言: 55 initials, 21 finals, 8 tones (33, 24, 53, 13, 55, 31, 53, 13). No remark on 重音/轻声 (unlike the Jiongnai paragraph on p.40 which says '轻声不明显').

sources.citation: Luo Xinggui 罗兴贵 & Yang Yadong 杨亚东. 2016 [2004]. 现代苗语概论：西部方言, ch. '苗语与苗语方言' (yuncunzhai.com online edition).
sources.note: Mentions 重安江次方言 distribution only (Huangping Fengtang, Chongxin; Kaili Longchang); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Fengxiang (West Hmongic) forms cited from Wang & Mao 1995 point 9 only; no Ge prosody statement (family-level p.199 'nominal prefixes are unstressed').

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, p.596.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Family-level only: 'Hmong-Mien is usually described as being exclusively tonal... we did not have access to sources that would allow us to elaborate on this point.' No Ge data.

sources.citation: Enwall, Joakim. 1998. Introductory remarks on M.H. Hutton's Keh Deo writing. Mon-Khmer Studies 28: 152-159.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.156: 'In Ge there are altogether six tones... some uncertainties regarding the tones of words appearing separately and in conjunction with other words, i.e. in tone sandhi environments.' Names the primary phonological sources: Wang Fushi 1979 Miaoyu fangyan shengyunmu bijiao (Fengxiang), Ni Gui & Li Yongsui 1959 fieldnotes, Hutton ms dictionary.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene (ed.); data Zhang Jimin 张济民 (Guizhou Institute of Nationalities), 2 Nov 1995. 'Ge / Changanjiang Miao' numerals. MPI-EVA Numeral Systems of the World's Languages (Wayback 2011).
sources.note: Numerals with tone values only (i33, a33, tsɪ31, plu33...); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (ed.). 1985. 苗语简志 Miaoyu jianzhi [A sketch of the Miao language]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. pp.106-107, 139 (scan leaves 111-112, 144).
sources.note: Nothing on stress for Chong'anjiang. p.106 gives extent/population of 重安江次方言 (c.40,000; Huangping Fengtang/Chongxin/Chongren, Kaili Longchang etc.); p.107: '连读变调现象除重安江次方言外都有' = Chong'anjiang is the only Chuanqiandian sub-dialect WITHOUT tone sandhi. Phonology chapter proper describes Dananshan only; the book's only 轻声 remark (p.12) concerns Xiangxi (Layiping) prefixes.

sources.citation: Sun Jin 孙金. 2020. 语言的谱系分类：黔东南枫香（亻革）语个案研究. PhD dissertation, 中南民族大学 South-Central Minzu University. 349 pp. (Glottolog ref 668106; Glottolog MED has '').
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only full-length modern description of Ge (Fengxiang) phonology; a 300+ page Chinese phonology thesis is the likeliest place for a 重音/轻声/词重音 remark. Glottolog evidently holds a PDF.

sources.citation: Li Yunbing 李云兵. 2018. 苗瑶语比较研究. 北京: 商务印书馆 (and Li Yunbing 2000 苗语方言划分遗留问题研究, 中央民族大学出版社).

sources.note: Most recent comparative treatment of all Miao sub-dialects incl. 重安江; its phonology chapters sometimes note 轻声/前缀弱化 per point.

sources.citation: Chen Xueyu 陈雪玉. 2011. 论东家话在苗语川黔滇方言中的地位 [On the position of Dongjia within the Chuanqiandian dialect of Miao]. MA thesis, 中央民族大学 Minzu University of China.

sources.note: Compares Dongjia (Majiang) and Gejia/Chong'anjiang phonology in detail; may contain syllable/prosody remarks for both Ge varieties.

sources.citation: Niederer, Barbara. 1998. Les langues Hmong-Mjen (Miáo-Yáo): phonologie historique. LINCOM Studies in Asian Linguistics 07. München: LINCOM Europa.

sources.note: Ch.2 gives phonological inventories with notes (tone sandhi, prefixes) for ~40 Hmong-Mien points including the Wang & Mao Fengxiang (Chong'anjiang) point; a French-language remark on accent/prefix atonicity is possible.
